messages.subject: discrete z or fill?
parts:
Greetings,

The fundamental problem appears to be converting a continuous variable to a discrete one. I'm not sure how I should expect to do this. I would expect this to be automatic, but that's clearly not happening.

The specific problem, I want to make a heat map like is given in the geom_tile examples but I want a discrete color scheme. In particular, I want to use a brewer scheme. Is this possible?

Here's what I've tried:

# set up
x11()
volcano3d <- melt(volcano)
names(volcano3d) <- c("x", "y", "z")

## contours on the continuous heat map
v <- ggplot(volcano3d, aes(x, y)) + geom_tile(aes(fill=z)) +
  stat_contour(aes(z=z))
v

## failure.
v <- ggplot(volcano3d, aes(x, y)) + geom_tile(aes(fill=z)) +
  stat_contour(aes(z=z)) +
  scale_fill_brewer(limits=c(90,200), breaks=((0:8)*13.75+90))
v

This last one fails with the message

Error: Continuous variable (z) supplied to discrete scale_brewer.

This seems to imply that I need to make the variable a factor before-hand.

I've also tried scale_fill_discrete() and it gives the same message replacing scale_brewer with scale_hue.

Same conclusion.

Question is: how to do this appropriately? Or some other way to achieve the same ends?

Thanks.

messages.author: e4aec126ff1dca22
messages.subject: Re: discrete z or fill?
parts: It's not pretty, but you can use scale_fill_gradientn() to make it work just fine :

volcano3d <- melt(volcano)
names(volcano3d) <- c('x','y','z')

ggplot(volcano3d, aes(x, y)) + geom_tile(aes(fill=z)) +
  stat_contour(aes(z=z)) +

scale_fill_gradientn(colours = brewer.pal(9, 'Set1'))

Cheers
david.

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: discrete z or fill?
parts:
> The fundamental problem appears to be converting a continuous variable to a
> discrete one. I'm not sure how I should expect to do this. I would expect
> this to be automatic, but that's clearly not happening.

I'm a little surprised that you expect that - there are many many
different ways of converting a continuous variable to a set of
discrete levels, and I think it's dangerous to choose one
automatically. You might want to have a look at the cut_number and
cut_interval functions for two ways of doing it by hand.

Hadley
